{{short description|none}}
In [[geometry]], [[isotoxal figure|isotoxal]] [[polyhedra]] and [[Tessellation|tiling]]s are defined by the property that they have symmetries taking any edge to any other edge.<ref>Peter R. Cromwell, ''[[Polyhedra (book)|Polyhedra]]'', Cambridge University Press 1997, {{isbn|0-521-55432-2}}, p.&nbsp;371</ref> Polyhedra with this property can also be called "edge-transitive", but they should be distinguished from [[edge-transitive graph]]s, where the symmetries are combinatorial rather than geometric.

[[Regular polyhedra]] are isohedral (face-transitive), isogonal (vertex-transitive), and isotoxal (edge-transitive).

[[Quasiregular polyhedron|Quasiregular]] polyhedra are isogonal and isotoxal, but not isohedral; their duals are isohedral and isotoxal, but not isogonal.

The dual of an isotoxal polyhedron is also an isotoxal polyhedron. (See the [[Dual polyhedron]] article.)

== Convex isotoxal polyhedra ==
The dual of a convex polyhedron is also a convex polyhedron.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=duality|url=http://maths.ac-noumea.nc/polyhedr/dual_.htm|access-date=2020-10-01|website=maths.ac-noumea.nc}}</ref>

There are nine [[Convex polyhedron|convex]] isotoxal polyhedra based on the [[Platonic solid]]s: the five (regular) Platonic solids, the two ([[Quasiregular polyhedron|quasiregular]]) common cores of dual Platonic solids, and their two duals.

The [[vertex figure]]s of the quasiregular forms are (squares or) rectangles; the vertex figures of the duals of the quasiregular forms are (equilateral triangles and equilateral triangles, or) equilateral triangles and squares, or equilateral triangles and regular pentagons.

== Isotoxal star-polyhedra ==
The dual of a non-convex polyhedron is also a non-convex polyhedron.<ref name=":0" /> (By contraposition.)

There are ten non-convex isotoxal polyhedra based on the [[Quasiregular polyhedron|quasiregular]] octahedron, cuboctahedron, and icosidodecahedron: the five (quasiregular) [[hemipolyhedra]] based on the quasiregular octahedron, cuboctahedron, and icosidodecahedron, and their five (infinite) duals:

== Isotoxal tilings of the hyperbolic plane ==

There are infinitely many isotoxal polygonal tilings of the hyperbolic plane, including the Wythoff constructions from the [[List of regular polytopes#Hyperbolic tilings|regular hyperbolic tilings]] {p,q}, and non-right (p q r) groups.

== Isotoxal tilings of the sphere ==

All isotoxal polyhedra listed above can be made as isotoxal tilings of the sphere.

In addition as spherical tilings, there are two other families which are degenerate as polyhedra. Even ordered hosohedron can be ''semiregular'', alternating two lunes, and thus isotoxal:
* [[hosohedron]] {2,q}
* [[dihedron]] {p,2}
